notes.title: JDM: Japanese Drift Master is now available!
notes.content:
We’ve got great news – our latest title:[url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/ ][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url], is now live on Steam!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/ 
[h3]This is a unique game born out of our deep love for cars and passion for Japanese culture.[/h3]

Get ready to explore the open world of Guntama – a city full of atmospheric streets, mountain passes, and iconic, fully licensed cars. Drift through the corners, tune your vehicles, and follow Touma’s journey through a story-rich manga-style narrative. All of that wrapped in a vibrant soundtrack and a visually engaging world.

If you’re craving fresh thrills and heart-pounding driving that rewards precision – now’s the perfect time to take the wheel!

Still not sure if it’s your thing? Check out the official launch trailer below and see what JDM is all about — we think you’ll feel the rush.

[previewyoutube=-iebhqKtmcg;full][/previewyoutube]

Gaming Factory

notes.title: JDM: Rise of the Scorpion is available now!
notes.content:
[h1]Hi,[/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35033617/70608a78d69c49fbfd5377c721ef23324ebe54b2.png[/img]

After months of hard work and dedication, the Gaming Factory team is thrilled to share what we've been working on. The F2P prologue to [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1153410/JDM_Japanese_Drift_Master/][b]JDM: Japanese Drift Master[/b][/url] - [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/1364930/JDM_Rise_of_the_Scorpion/][b]JDM: Rise of the Scorpion[/b][/url] - is finally available! See you on the track,

notes.title: Back2School - big discounts and a bundle
notes.content:
[h1]Hello![/h1]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/cb1309be5ca688bafd8b13b5ab5989cd689c9826.png[/img]

[h3]Holidays are over, it's time to go back to school. After school though it's best to relax a bit and have some fun. We have prepared for you a bundle great for that and of course the discount for this game.[/h3]

https://store.steampowered.com/bundle/27707/Back2School/

[h3]Here are the games you will get in the bundle:[/h3]
[b][list]
[*] Bakery Simulator
[*] ZooKeeper
[*] Bug Academy + Dlc (Artistic Kit)
[*] Sapper - Defuse the Bomb Simulator
[*] Gallic Wars - Battle Simulator
[*] Commander '85
[*] Pangeon
[*] Foodtruck Arena
[*] Bouncy Bob: Episode 2
[*] Gunslingers & Zombies
[/list][/b]
 1. [b]Bug Academy + Dlc (Artistic Kit))[/b] where you learn [b]Physics[/b]- How the furniture in the apartment reacts when a refrigerator enters it through the window, [b]Mathematics[/b] - Calculating the angle account when throwing cows to the fence, and [b]Art[/b] - Painting pictures while having fun with tossing cows and smashing everything.

2. [b]ZooKeeper [/b] where you learn [b]Natural Sciences[/b] - different animal species, their reactions, and characteristics and [b]Business Studies[/b] - the basics of ZOO, animals, and staff management while having the pleasure of watching animals and creating your own zoo

3. [b]Bakery Simulator[/b] where you learn [b]Cooking[/b] - Baking to be precise. You will get a basic knowledge how what the baking process looks like and you find out what kind of machines bakers use and have fun baking your favorite bread in the game and then doing it in real life! 

4. [b]Sapper - Defuse the Bomb Simulator[/b] where you learn [b]Technology[/b] - many kinds of bombs that can be found nowadays, how to disarm them, and how dangerous the sapper's job can really be and have fun searching for a bomb and having the thrill of disarming it just in time.

5. [b]Gallic Wars - Battle Simulator[/b] where you learn [b]History[/b] - Never heard of ancient times? Romans, Gauls? Those two nations didn't like each other too much. [b]Physics[/b] - what can happen if a catapult's stone hit a big group of units? Have fun using magic, traps, and catapults.

6.[b] Commander '85[/b] where you learn [b]History[/b] - Experience what it was like in the 1980s. How some feared war and feared new technologies coming into our lives... The rise of computers [b]Science[/b] - Find out how computers worked in the 1980s, and how hard it was to operate them compared to the present while having fun with challenging gameplay, where there are no tutorials, no help, no easy solutions. There is only you, a small monitor screen, and commands.

7. [b]Pangeon[/b] where you learn [b]IT[/b] - how to use only pixels, that create blurry pictures to make a game in the times of hyper-realistic graphics while having fun searching the dungeons and killing monsters.

8. [b]Foodtruck Arena[/b] where you learn [b]PE[/b] - In most physical challenges, good cooperation is always vital. It is not different here. Arena, football, cars, cooperation. That's quite a good combo to get a lot of fun.

9. [b]Bouncy Bob: Episode 2[/b] where you learn what to do on [b]School break[/b] - how to cope with your friends when no one tells you what to do or not do!

10. [b]Gunslingers & Zombies[/b] - Face Zombie Apocalypse in Wild West. Manage your crew in a Turn-based strategy and adventure game. Survive, scavenge, and explore the world. Use the different talents of your team members and develop your tactics. Resolve the zombie mystery.


[h3]When your mom comes in saying "stop playing, it's time to learn something" - you just need to show this.[/h3]

[h3]One more thing... Check our upcoming game Electrician Simulator![/h3]
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1080020/Electrician_Simulator/

[h3]Good Luck and Have Fun, fellow gamers! :)[/h3]

notes.title: Gauls Gathering
notes.content:
[h2]Even in ancient times tribes needed a good intel to know when they are being invaded.[/h2]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/cb89f4ed49e0a31db155f3efbcf41613be7d9a32.png[/img]

Gauls have their spies inside the Roman newspaper. 

[u][b]Three times a day [/b][/u](except weekends when lazy Romans rest) you'll get swift and short info about what is going on.

[url=https://twitter.com/GamingFactory6][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/419f6649f866ba47e7405fb1747284cae1d6a824.png[/img][/url]

But that's not all. Our best spy filtered out the Romans' headquarters. [u][b]Twice a day[/b][/u] he is sending us comprehensive information on the movements of the Roman forces and their allies.

[url=https://www.facebook.com/gamingfactorysa][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/fa5037f617ba42874f5be860bf0a8301d93632a8.png[/img][/url]

]Sometimes it can be a problem as many Gauls do not know how to read. But do not worry, we have our man in their propaganda bulletin. [u][b]Once a day [/b][/u](except weekend - these lazy ba...rds) we can check their plans on a graphic image.

[url=https://www.instagram.com/gamingfactoryofficial/][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/ca6549ffeedb48a79a5c7e1675083479fcf9273e.png[/img][/url]


Knowing the news is one thing... but sharing it is another. To win against Roman Empire we need to gather our forces, study enemy tactics, and comment/decide what to do to stop them. 

[url=https://discord.gg/ZyKJBvN][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/777f33df63be70dbd62d33a37aec47bdd1f5914a.png[/img][/url]


[h3]Join mighty Gauls in their path to freedom.[/h3]

notes.title: DevLog#2
notes.content:
[u][b]Deploying units and watching them fight is fun.[/b][/u]

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/988634a50f374f8c60952073e74607c596514ccd.png[/img]

There is something very satisfying about just watching the mayhem that you somewhat planned, but I wanted to include the player in the fighting part of the game. So I added magic that player can use during a battle.

I used the same mechanics for items like traps, abatis and other helpful junk that will be placed on the battlefield during the deployment phase.

To access these the player will use a new inventory panel. Magic spells and other items will be valuable and scarce, so 10 inventory slots will probably be enough.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/2b711a4a9789f9799f5c607aa2b196bcb22643a0.png[/img]

Easy and recognizable way to scale these types of mechanics is using “common, rare and legendary” descriptions.. No need to reinvent the wheel. Most people understand this type of scaling and their corresponding colors: gray, blue and gold

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/c06d93e8e07e3f838eaf8b09c8be53560f2ce441.png[/img]

At this point there are 2 spells and 1 trap implemented.

[b]FIREBALL[/b]
Simple mechanics. Very useful for destroying groups of enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/5d83e02a1b716c58b3f088f4f7a3d90dae47eff1.gif[/img]

[b]GUT GRANADE[/b]
My favourite so far. You cast it on one of your units and send it to the battle. The moment affected unit comes close to an enemy unit it detonates, killing all enemies in the explosion’s radius.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/24e9090b02a39aec911b5182db1eaabb919fd318.gif[/img]

[b]TRAP[/b]
Nothing fancy about it. Player places it on the ground in the predicted path of enemy troops. Kills all in range.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/3684c45bca5fba41e32faf9b748f756ab6342eb5.gif[/img]

notes.title: Announcement#1
notes.content:
As you have already seen the name has changed from Siege Machines Builder to Gallic Wars: Battle Simulator.

First of all, the background to the game is the war between the Roman legions and a horde of invincible Gauls. In this war there was [b]no need to use siege weapons[/b].    

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/0a6e8cbe1465d9815f0adcf799daffde74c1d364.jpg][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/7f88335806f00eb401ea2e3749bda79fe79dbc89.jpg[/img][/url]

Gauls only had some palisades, trees and tents. Roman Legions were strong enough to oppose them using just arrows, pikes and swords. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/8cdea424ab894db91f810f8c03541d567de7df64.gif[/img]

Secondly from the day 1 the game has grown. If you say the game looks like TABS, you are not far off, but... we want this game to be better, larger ... and historically accurate... a bit. 


The most important is the fun... who doesn't like Asterix & Obelix? Who cares these characters were made up. It's all about the fun... We are trying to prepare for you a game that above all gives pleasure.

Stay tuned,

More content is coming soon.
Gaming Factory

notes.title: DevLog#1
notes.content:
Hello fellow Gallic Warriors,

At this point the game has 6 types of units. All have their own animations and textures (with some overlap). To make them appear different and organic they also have different looking equipment and accessories.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/51ea190228e0153f70964db1ef948f32553af4db.jpg[/img]

To limit the amount of work on creating units in the game I hacked a couple of things. 

Creating separate models with animations and textures seemed unreasonable – they look pretty similar. So I created one model with 22 animations, 2 base textures (Gallic and Roman) and a couple of overlay textures.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/cfc274894c1311518c7df0836f138c437ca5e860.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/cfc274894c1311518c7df0836f138c437ca5e860.gif[/img][/url]

This way I have only one blender file, so resources are not wasted and every change in the exported file I have to make – I make once.

[url={STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/2b57709d82d56992299beb5dda979809f3caedd2.gif][img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/2b57709d82d56992299beb5dda979809f3caedd2.gif[/img][/url]

Accessories, equipment and materials are not a part of base mesh – they are randomised and instantiated at runtime. 

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/34901461/be7f51f5e9c1c8e59498fe387f5ac95fd4782482.jpg[/img]

And for final effect units are slightly scaled, so they don’t look like clones.
